price.quote: Its significant 400-pound weight capacity is impressive, and the option to choose between a high-step and step-through frame adds to its versatility. For those wanting a bit more tech, there’s also a torque sensor model priced at $1,699 (which is the bike we tested).
price.basis: price at time of review (torque-sensor model)

cls.quote: The Himiway D5 Zebra delivered a solid performance in our Electric Bike Report Speed Test, equipped with a torque sensor and a 750W rear hub motor. Since the D5 Zebra can be switched between class 2 and class 3 speeds, it was tested in both settings to fully evaluate its capabilities.
cls.basis: switchable Class 2/3 with throttle; EBR's class box lists Class 1, 2 and 3. Recorded 2 assuming it ships at 20 mph (maker says '20+ Mph')

cls.quote: Discover that Himiway e-bikes have the capability to operate as technically Class 3 e-bikes. While both of these bikes are shipped as Class 2 ebikes, users have the option to unlock the speed limiter, increasing the max speed to 25mph
cls.basis: Himiway's 'Unlock the Limit of the Speed' page: ships as Class 2, unlockable; its per-model unlock list includes 'D5 (Torque Sensor), D5 Plus (Rhino), D7 1000w, Rambler, Rambler Upgraded: watch video'

cls.quote: Max speed: 20 mph ⟶ e-Bike class: Class 2
cls.basis: Upway refurbished 2022 Himiway Zebra, closed (high-step) frame, 960 Wh, 86 Nm, 750 W

spd.quote: CLASS 2 (THROTTLE TO 20 MPH) ⟶ CLASS 3 (PEDAL ASSIST TO 28 MPH)

tq.quote: The Himiway D5 Zebra, armed with a 750W rear hub motor and fairly significant torque output of 86 Nm, entered our ‘Hell Hole’ hill test with the expectation of solid climbing ability.

wh.quote: Battery: 960 Wh, 48V Samsung Cells ⟶ Display: Full-Color LCD Display

range.quote: Kicking things off with the minimal pedal assist (PAS 1), the D5 Zebra gave us an impressive 69.96 miles on a single charge. This test included a climb of 1,253 feet in elevation and lasted 5 hours and 34 minutes, all while maintaining an average speed of 12.57 mph. | Shifting to maximum pedal assist (PAS 5), the D5 Zebra covered 54.24 miles at a higher average speed of 18.1 mph spanning 3 hours and climbing an elevation of 1,046 feet.

wt.quote: Tested Weight: 76.8 lbs ⟶ Rider height range: 5′3″ ~ 6′5″

load.quote: Total payload capacity: 400 lb. ⟶ COMPONENTS & ACCESSORIES

motor.quote: Powering this beast is a hefty 48V, 960Wh battery paired with a 750W rear hub motor, delivering a solid 85 Newton Meters (Nm) of torque. I could feel the power right away as the large Kenda 26×4” tires effortlessly rolled over everything in their path.

height.quote: Rider height range: 5′3″ ~ 6′5″ ⟶ Total payload capacity: 400 lb.

notes: Maker regular price $2,299, on sale $1,499 (EBR's review quoted $1,699 for the torque-sensor model at the time). Maker gives top speed only as '20+ Mph' and no class; Electric Bike Report says it switches between Class 2 and 3 speeds, so cls 2 / 20 mph assumes 20 mph out of the box (adjustable to 28 mph). Torque: maker and EBR hill test say 86 Nm; EBR's intro says 85 Nm. Maker spec standover line lists both ST and SO frames on this page. electricbikereview.com search returned no results for Himiway. | recheck: Himiway's own 'Unlock the Limit of the Speed' page says its e-bikes ship as Class 2 (unlockable to 25 mph) and lists this model's unlock video; 1 WebSearch used for the Himiway set. Upway refurbished Zebra listings (2021-2025) all say 20 mph / Class 2.
